summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, insulin-dependent diabetes, and prior MSSA leg infection was admitted for left lower extremity erythema and swelling concerning for recurrent cellulitis. He had elevated white count and lactate on admission but negative blood and imaging studies for abscess or DVT. IV vancomycin was started, later broadened to Zosyn. A skin biopsy showed findings indeterminate between early cellulitis and small vessel vasculitis, with a fungal culture positive for Pityrosporum yeast likely as a contaminant. The patient improved clinically with treatment, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with a PICC line for a two-week course of IV vancomycin and Zosyn, plus one week of oral Bactrim. Insulin regimen was adjusted for improved glycemic control, azathioprine was held, and follow-up was arranged with rheumatology and infectious disease.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
